title: how can this possibly be possibly lost memory? valgrind
body_html:
I use valgrind to detect memory lost, and I know that possibly lost should be treated as definitely lost, however, I have this very simple program, and how can it possibly lose memory? I do not randomly allocate any pointer in the middle of nowhere..

First, I write a function to create a fresh string of arbitrary size: (allocate memory, then set all the values in the array to 0, end it with a 0. this is as clean as it could be, in my opinion.)

#include <stdlib.h>

char    *ft_strnew(size_t size)
{
    char    *str;
    size_t  i;

    str = (char*)malloc(sizeof(char) * (size + 1));
    if (str == NULL)
        return (str);
    i = 0;
    while (i < size)
    str[i++] = '\0';
    str[i] = '\0';
    return (str);
}

Then I use this function 

#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

char *ft_strnew(size_t size);

int main()
{
    char *s;
    s = ft_strnew(2);
    s[0] = 'a';
    s[1] = 'b';
    s[2] = 0;
    free(s);
    return 0;
}

If I don't free(s) valgrind says I definitely lose 3 bytes. Now it put free(s) and valgrind says I definitely lose 0 byte.

  1. However, it always says I possibly lose 72 bytes. What does it mean? How to fix it?
  2. At the end of the report, it says 2 errors, what are those errors?
  3. How to fix the 'still reachable'? Is it important?

Delete the a.out file and try again. It seems to be a complete different program.

weird. i delete a.out, i put them in new directory and compile again.. still.......

regarding: str = (char*)malloc(sizeof(char) * (size + 1)); 1) the expression: sizeof(char) is defined in the C standard as 1. Multiplying anything by 1 has absolutely no effect. Suggest removing that expression. 2) the returned type from the heap allocation functions: malloc calloc realloc is void* which can be assigned to any pointer. Casting the returned value just clutters the code, making it more difficult to understand, debug, etc. Suggest removing that cast.

regarding: if (str == NULL) return (str); When the call to malloc() fails, a NULL pointer is returned to main(). main() starts writing to that pointer. When malloc() fails, this will result in a seg fault event. Suggest using: if (str == NULL) { perror( "malloc failed" ); exit( EXIT_FAILURE ); }
Suggest replacing the call to malloc() with a call to calloc() and removing these statements: while (i < size) str[i++] = '\0'; str[i] = '\0';
regarding: ` i = 0;     while (i < size)`  Strongly suggest replacing with: `for( size_t i =0; i < size; i++ )
the error report says: 179 allocs, 17 frees, but the posted code only shows 1 alloc and 1 free. Please correct the posted code or replace the error report with the real one,

thank you for all the added information. this code is written with the norm in my school. also, people say that i run this on mac so there is something messing with valgrind and the possibly lost memory report is not due to my program
